title: Single-molecule strong optomechanical regimes in SERS via hybrid plasmonic cavities
authors: Miguel Á. Martínez-García, Johannes Feist, Diego Martín-Cano
abstract: We identify enhanced strong coherent Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering (SERS) interactions facilitated by hybridized metallo-dielectric cavities with a resonant fluorescent molecule. By illuminating a detuned electronic transition near saturation via a narrowband hybrid plasmonic mode, we observe enhanced splittings in the Stokes and anti-Stokes spectra, revealing strong optomechanical coupling and nonlinear vibrational modifications at intensities far below irreversible SERS damage thresholds. We compute the second-order photon correlations that allows identifying the nonclassical character associated to these strong optomechanical interactions and SERS configurations that enables them to optically characterize the anharmonic character of the vibrational modes.
summary: The paper develops a theoretical framework to study strong optomechanical coupling at the single-molecule level using SERS enhanced by hybrid plasmonic cavities. By analyzing photon correlations, the authors show that nonclassical signatures like antibunching can be used to optically characterize anharmonic vibrational potentials in molecules. This advances the field toward quantum control of molecular vibrations.
main_problem: The research aims to achieve and characterize single-molecule strong optomechanical coupling within Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering (SERS) regimes, overcoming limitations posed by weak interactions and sample damage at high intensities.
main_result: Strong coupling is demonstrated using detuned emitter-hybrid cavity configurations, allowing the observation of enhanced spectral splittings and nonclassical photon statistics that reveal anharmonic vibrational modifications at single-molecule levels.
method: The study employs open-system quantum dynamics simulations using Lindblad master equations to model dissipation in a coupled system, supplemented by calculating second-order photon correlation functions.
model_or_system: The physical platform is a hybrid plasmonic cavity coupled to fluorescent molecules. The system is modeled via an electron-vibron Hamiltonian incorporating coupling terms ($g_{om}$) and analyzed using master equations for dissipation ($\dot{\hat{ho}}$).
key_observables: Enhanced splittings in Stokes/anti-Stokes spectra, nonclassical photon statistics (bunching/antibunching), and violation of the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality.
important_parameters: Strong coupling regime where coherent energy exchange dominates dissipation; driving powers ($\Omega/2\pi \sim 1-10$ THz); cavity enhancement factor ($g_{hyb}/\kappa_{hyb}$).
main_assumptions: The Markovian description of decay into environmental baths is assumed, and the use of a detuned emitter-hybrid cavity configuration is crucial to avoid high intensities.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the hybrid cavity structure and energy levels; spectral maps show Stokes/anti-Stokes sidebands vs. driving strength ($\Omega$); $g^{(2)}$ maps compare resonant vs. cooperative models, highlighting nonclassical correlations for anharmonic vibrations.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the physical model (Hamiltonian/Master Equation), demonstrating how detuning enables strong coupling below damage thresholds, and finally using photon correlation measurements ($g^{(2)}$) to spectroscopically probe nonlinear vibrational potentials via antibunching signatures.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges quantum optics with molecular spectroscopy by proposing a method to use single-photon statistics (antibunching) as an optical signature for anharmonicity, which is a core topic in advanced AMO physics and open quantum systems.
